page.title: Declaration Registry
page.purpose: Show every consumer-declared record in the fleet with its registration state, so a broken or colliding declaration is visible here rather than only at generation time.

states.description: At least one declaration failed to parse; its error is shown and the service is running normally.
Two declarations claim one key; both paths are named and neither wins.
A declaration file was deleted; the record is retained and refuses new generation.
No consumer has declared any record yet.
Data for this surface is in flight; skeleton structure is shown rather than a blank frame.
Some data resolved and some did not; what resolved stays usable and what failed is named rather than silently omitted.
Displayed data is known to be out of date relative to its source; the surface says so rather than presenting it as current.
The request failed; the specific cause is stated inline and the surface offers the action that retries it.

claims.statement: An invalid declaration is perceivably distinct from an unhealthy service, and the surface makes clear the system is running normally.
claims.rationale: A malformed consumer file must never read as this scenario being down; it must never block startup either. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: A key collision names both claiming paths and states that neither was applied.
claims.rationale: Last-writer-wins is refused by design, so the surface must show why nothing resolved rather than appearing stuck. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: Every declared record shows its owning scenario and file path.
claims.rationale: The file is the source of truth; a record whose origin is not visible cannot be fixed by the team that owns it. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: An unregistered record is distinct from a deleted one and still resolves historical provenance.
claims.rationale: Hard-deleting would orphan the provenance of every candidate ever generated from it. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)
